node.title: feat(crates)!: split the crate graph by domain and open the event log

steps.task:
## What

The first of four steps on one branch that redraws printobserver's crate graph by
domain. This step **opens the event log**: the closed `EventKind`/`EventPayload` pair in
`printobserver-types` — one variant per domain's events, so that the supervision core
matched on Obico's kinds by name and every domain's payload struct sat in the crate every
other crate builds against — becomes an envelope with an open kind name and an opaque
payload, and **every event kind moves to the crate of the domain that owns it**. The
supervision core reacts to the vision port's `NormalizedAlert` and to nothing an adapter
declares; the store persists exactly the bytes it persists today; the contract codegen
learns the open envelope, reads every `schemas/<crate>/` directory, and still emits every
domain's payload type to the three clients. No type that is not an event kind moves in
this step — the provider wire types, the printer vocabulary, the supervision records and
the store port are the later steps' — so that this step is one thing: who owns the log's
kinds, and what a reader of the log may assume.

### The target crate graph, which every step of this node builds toward

This node's four steps share one branch and one contract: the graph below, and the event
seam stated after it. A step builds toward it and never past it; a step that finds it wants
a different cut — a missing item, a different owner, a better name for something a
criterion fixes — surfaces a proposal to the manager over the ask seam and keeps building
against this one, because the steps after it and the change request's reviewer are reading
this table. A shared interface is never changed unilaterally.

Thirteen crates become twelve. `printobserver-store-api` is retired from the workspace:
release automation publishes every workspace crate, so it stays on crates.io at `0.2.0`,
is never yanked, and is never published again. The manager measured its consumers before
this plan was written: crates.io's reverse-dependency listings for `printobserver-types`
(11), `printobserver-store-api` (5) and the three other port crates name only crates of
this workspace; a GitHub code search for `printobserver-types` across the owner's
repositories returns only this repository; no other checkout registered on this host
names them. So the API this refactor breaks has no consumer outside this tree, and the
one release it cuts is a pre-1.0 breaking release (`feat!` → `0.3.0`). Do not re-derive
that measurement.

| Crate | Owns after the refactor | May depend on (workspace crates, every dependency table) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `printobserver-types` | **The cross-domain contract, and only that** — what every domain and every client must agree on, and nothing a domain adding a concept has to edit. The identity rule: the `identifier!` macro (exported), `IdentifierError`, the UUID-v7 rule, and the three identifiers the envelope reaches — `PrintId`, `EventId`, `ImageId`. The representation rules: `Timestamp`, `RawBytes`, `FileName`, `Reported<T>` and `Range`. The event envelope: `EventKind`, `EventSource`, `EventBody`, the `EventPayload` trait, `EventRecord`, and `ImageRef` (the envelope's image handle). The schema toolkit (`contract`: `Sample`, `TypeContract`, `WireField`, `wire_fields`, `schema_of`, `event_schema_of`, and a `declared` set naming only this crate's own types). The `serde`, `serde_json` and `schemars` re-exports. Its module doc says it is the vocabulary every domain and every client must agree on, and that a type belongs here only if adding or changing one domain's concept does not require editing it. | — |
| `printobserver-printer-api` | The printer port, plus the printer domain's vocabulary: `PrinterSnapshot`, `HeaterSnapshot`, `JobSnapshot`, `PrinterState`, `Adjustable` and `AdjustableError`, the seven `*_RANGE` constants, `RangedField` and `RANGED_FIELDS`. | `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-vision-api` | The vision port: `NormalizedAlert` (now carrying an `EventBody` and a provider-neutral `ProviderPrint` correlation), `FetchedImage`, `VisionError`, `VisionPort`; and the event kind `malformed_external_event` (`MalformedExternalEventPayload`) — a body this port could not read, written down. | `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-supervisor-api` | The supervisor port, plus its vocabulary: `SupervisionSession`, `SessionPhase`, `AgentAssessment`, `Confidence`; and the event kinds `supervision_session_opened` and `supervision_session_closed`. | `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-core` | **The supervision domain.** Its logic, as now; its own records: `PrintRecord` (whose external correlation field is `provider_print_id`), `ManifestNarrowing`, `JobManifest`, `PrintContext`, `Intervention`, `InterventionOutcome`, `ImageRecord`, `SafetyEnvelope`, `EffectiveBounds`, `PolicyDecision`, `RejectionReason`, `PrintAction`, `ActionKind`, `Actor`, `ActorClass`, `ExecutionOutcome`, `AcknowledgementDisposition`, `ActionRequest`, `ActionRecord`, and its own identifiers `ActionId` and `InterventionId` (minted through the exported macro); its event kinds `action_requested`, `action_executed`, `action_rejected`, `intervention_expired`, `agent_assessment`, `operator_acknowledgement`, `port_failure` (with `PortFailureSite`); its event-source names `system`, `operator`, `agent`; and the persistence interfaces it needs, one trait per aggregate rather than one trait for everything, with the shapes those methods carry — `EventDraft`, `HistoryQuery`, `ImageLookup`, `SettleOutcome`, `AuditPage`, `StoreError`, `DEFAULT_HISTORY_WINDOW`, `MAX_HISTORY_LIMIT`, `resolve_history_limit` — and the four behavioural facts of the history read, stated where the traits are. | `printobserver-types`, `printobserver-printer-api`, `printobserver-vision-api`, `printobserver-supervisor-api` — and **no adapter crate**, which is what keeps the graph acyclic |
| `printobserver-octoprint` | The OctoPrint adapter — unchanged. | `printobserver-printer-api`, `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-obico` | The Obico adapter: its nine wire types (`ObicoEventType`, `ObicoFailureAlert`, `ObicoFailureEvent`, `ObicoFailureEventType`, `ObicoNotificationEvent`, `ObicoPrintInfo`, `ObicoPrinterInfo`, `ObicoPrinterNotification`, `ObicoTimestamp`) and the webhook sample bodies; its event kinds `obico_failure_alert` and `obico_printer_notification` with `ObicoNotificationType`; its event-source name `obico`; the vision port implementation; and the webhook ingress, which writes through the supervision domain's store traits. | `printobserver-vision-api`, `printobserver-core`, `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-oneharness` | The oneharness adapter — unchanged. | `printobserver-supervisor-api`, `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-store-sqlite` | The SQLite implementation (and the in-memory one beside it) of core's store traits. | `printobserver-core`, `printobserver-supervisor-api`, `printobserver-printer-api`, `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-server` | The composition root and the HTTP surface — as now; and the event kind `startup_reconciliation` (`StartupReconciliationPayload`, `StartupOutcome`), which its reconcile module alone writes. | every crate above |
| `printobserver-sdk` | The generated Rust client. | — |
| `printobserver` | The command — unchanged. | `printobserver-server`, `printobserver-sdk`, `printobserver-types` |

Four consequences the table is drawn for, which the finished tree shows:

- A change to one provider's wire format **or to one provider's event payload** edits that
  provider's crate and rebuilds it and the composition roots. The reverse-dependency set
  of `printobserver-octoprint`, `printobserver-obico` and `printobserver-oneharness` is
  exactly `{printobserver-server, printobserver}`; of `printobserver-store-sqlite` the
  same.
- `printobserver-types` still sits under every crate — that is what a contract crate is —
  but nothing in it names a domain: no enum with a variant per provider or per domain's
  events, no list of kinds, no list of sources. A domain that adds an event kind, an
  aggregate or a source name edits its own crate and regenerates the clients; it edits
  nothing central. That is the test the sharpened `code_lands_in_the_domain_that_owns_it`
  rule applies, and this graph is drawn to pass it.
- The event log is **open**. A reader of the log — the store, the server, a client, a
  test — handles a kind it does not know explicitly rather than by exhaustive match: it
  carries the record through, filters by name, or reads a typed payload out of it and
  gets nothing back when the kind is another's. Exhaustive matching over the log is gone
  from this workspace, by design.
- The SDK contract is the schema set under `schemas/<crate>/<Type>.json`, keyed by type
  name across every declaring crate, and the codegen reads every crate directory; a type
  moving crates moves its schema file between directories and changes no generated line.
  The generated clients change in exactly one respect across the whole branch: they say
  what the server says about the log — the envelope is open, every domain's payload type
  is still emitted, and a kind→payload table with a typed accessor replaces the closed
  union.

### The event seam, which every step builds to

Declared in `printobserver-types` (module `event`, re-exported at the root). The names,
shapes and wire forms below are the contract; the exact error type an accessor answers,
the derive lists, and the constructor spellings are the implementer's, stated in the code's
own docs. Every crate that declares an event kind restates nothing from here: it imports
the trait and the envelope, and the **one authoritative source of a kind name is the
`KIND` const on the payload type that owns it** — the schema marker is written from that
const by the toolkit, the store column is written from it, and the clients' tables are
generated from the marker, with the drift gate (`check-generated`) going red when the
generated copy parts from the schema set.

```rust
/// The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the
/// domain that owns the event. Serializes as the bare string; schema: string, pattern
/// `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Ord + Hash, so a filter can hold a set of them.
pub struct EventKind(String);            // EventKind::new(impl Into<String>), as_str(), Display

/// Where an event came from, as the bare string each domain declares for itself.
/// The four names in use today are unchanged: "obico", "operator", "agent", "system".
pub struct EventSource(String);          // same shape as EventKind

/// One typed payload declared under a kind name, by the domain that owns it.
pub trait EventPayload: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema {
    const KIND: &'static str;
    fn kind() -> EventKind { EventKind::new(Self::KIND) }
}

/// The kind and the payload, as the log holds them: the pair `{"kind": .., "payload": ..}`.
pub struct EventBody { pub kind: EventKind, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
impl EventBody {
    pub fn of<P: EventPayload>(payload: &P) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error>;
    pub fn is<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> bool;                        // kind == P::KIND
    pub fn read<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>; // None: another's kind
}

/// One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it. Wire form unchanged:
/// `id`, `print_id`, `source`, `received_at`, `image`, `kind`, `payload`, `raw`.
pub struct EventRecord {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub print_id: Option<PrintId>,
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: Option<RawBytes>,
}
impl EventRecord {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &EventKind;
    pub fn payload_as<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>;
}

// In the schema toolkit (`contract`): the schema of an event payload is the schema its type
// emits plus one top-level member, `"x-event-kind": P::KIND`. Nothing writes that member by
// hand; the owning crate's schema test writes and reconciles the file through this.
pub fn event_schema_of<P: EventPayload>() -> serde_json::Value;
```

The thirteen kind names are wire and storage contract and do not change: `obico_failure_alert`,
`obico_printer_notification`, `malformed_external_event`, `action_requested`,
`action_executed`, `action_rejected`, `intervention_expired`, `supervision_session_opened`,
`supervision_session_closed`, `agent_assessment`, `operator_acknowledgement`,
`port_failure`, `startup_reconciliation` — each the `KIND` const of the payload type the
table above assigns to its owner. Kind names are unique across the workspace, and the
codegen is the cross-domain check: it refuses two schemas carrying the same `x-event-kind`.

Two other shapes carry the seam across boundaries and are part of it:

```rust
// printobserver-vision-api — what an adapter hands the supervision domain. Core reads the
// correlation here and never a provider's payload by kind.
pub struct NormalizedAlert {
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: RawBytes,
    pub image_url: Option<String>,
    /// The provider's own identifier for the print this alert is about, and the file it named,
    /// when the alert is about a print at all.
    pub print: Option<ProviderPrint>,
}
pub struct ProviderPrint { pub id: i64, pub file_name: Option<String> }

// The store's own draft of an event (in printobserver-store-api until step 3, in
// printobserver-core from then on):
pub struct EventDraft { pub print_id: Option<PrintId>, pub source: EventSource,
                        pub received_at: Timestamp, #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
                        pub raw: Option<RawBytes> }
// HistoryQuery.kinds becomes Vec<EventKind>; empty still means every kind.
```

**Persistence is unchanged, and that is the fact the whole cut rests on.** The SQLite
`events` table already holds `kind TEXT` as the bare kind name and `payload TEXT` as the
JSON text of the pair `{"kind":"<kind>","payload":{...}}` (what the closed enum's tagged
form serialized to); the open store writes the identical text — `kind` from `body.kind`,
`payload` as the JSON of `body` — and reads a record back off the `payload` column. A row
written by 0.2.0 reads under 0.3.0 unchanged, and a row whose kind no crate of this
workspace declares reads back as an `EventRecord` carrying it. The `source` column already
holds the bare source string.

**The generated clients' contract**, produced by `tools/contract-codegen` from the schema set:
`EventRecord` in each client is the envelope — `kind: string` and an opaque `payload`
(Rust `serde_json::Value`, Python `object`, TypeScript `unknown`) beside the fields above;
`EventSource` is a string; every payload type whose schema carries `x-event-kind` is
emitted as a standalone type whether or not an operation reaches it; each client carries a
generated table from kind name to payload type and a typed accessor that answers the
payload as that type for a matching kind and nothing for another, with no other runtime
validation than today's clients perform; a kind from a newer server flows through. The
package names — the `printobserver-sdk` crate, the `printobserver-sdk` wheel,
`@printobserver/sdk` — do not change.

The dependency rule is stated as this table, not as layers. `repo-policy.toml`'s
`[crates]` section becomes an explicit per-crate list of the workspace crates each crate
may depend on (across `dependencies`, `dev-dependencies` and `build-dependencies`), and
`tools/repo-checks`'s workspace check refuses any workspace edge the table does not admit
and any table row naming a crate the workspace lacks — the step that draws an edge is the
step that admits it in the table, so the check-repo tier proves the target graph rather
than a later step. Until step 3 replaces it, the layered rule in force today permits every
edge the steps before it draw.

### What this step does

1. **The seam, in `printobserver-types`.** `event.rs` declares `EventKind`, `EventSource`,
   the `EventPayload` trait, `EventBody`, `EventRecord` and `event_schema_of` exactly in
   the shape the seam section states; the enum `EventPayload`, the enum `EventKind` with
   its `ALL`, the enum `EventSource`, and every `*Payload` struct, `ObicoNotificationType`,
   `PortFailureSite` and `StartupOutcome` leave this crate. `ImageRef` stays: the envelope
   carries it. The crate's `declared` set names what it still declares, its schema test
   writes `EventRecord.json`, `EventKind.json`, `EventSource.json` (now a string schema)
   and the rest, and `schemas/printobserver-types/` holds no file for a type the crate no
   longer declares. The module docs of `lib.rs` and `event.rs` say what the envelope is,
   why it is open, and that a type belongs in this crate only if adding or changing one
   domain's concept does not require editing it. `tests/event_pairs.rs` — the walk over
   every ordered pair of kinds proving the closed pair closed — is replaced by tests of
   the seam: a payload read back under its own kind, nothing read back under another's,
   a record carrying a kind nothing declares surviving a round trip, the pair's wire form,
   and the schema marker `event_schema_of` writes.

2. **Every kind to its owner**, each with its `Sample` impl, its `EventPayload` impl
   naming its `KIND` (the same string that was its tag), its schema file written by the
   owning crate's `tests/schemas.rs` through `event_schema_of` into
   `schemas/<crate>/<Type>.json`, and the tests that prove it:
   - `ObicoFailureAlertPayload`, `ObicoPrinterNotificationPayload`, `ObicoNotificationType`
     → `printobserver-obico`, which also declares its source name (`"obico"`) as a
     constant the server's ingress uses for an unauthenticated post. The crate gains a
     `tests/schemas.rs` reconciling `schemas/printobserver-obico/` (copy the port crates'
     `tests/support/schema_files.rs` reconciler, as the previous plan's step did).
   - `MalformedExternalEventPayload` → `printobserver-vision-api`, beside
     `VisionError::Malformed`, whose written-down form it is.
   - `SupervisionSessionOpenedPayload`, `SupervisionSessionClosedPayload` →
     `printobserver-supervisor-api`.
   - `ActionRequestedPayload`, `ActionExecutedPayload`, `ActionRejectedPayload`,
     `InterventionExpiredPayload`, `AgentAssessmentPayload`,
     `OperatorAcknowledgementPayload`, `PortFailurePayload`, `PortFailureSite` →
     `printobserver-core`, which also declares the source names `"system"`, `"operator"`
     and `"agent"`. Core gains a `tests/schemas.rs` reconciling `schemas/printobserver-core/`.
     These payloads still reference `PrintAction`, `Actor`, `PolicyDecision`,
     `InterventionOutcome`, `Adjustable`, `AgentAssessment` where they live today, in
     `printobserver-types`; the later steps move those.
   - `StartupReconciliationPayload`, `StartupOutcome` → `printobserver-server`, whose
     `reconcile.rs` is their only writer; the server's existing `tests/schemas.rs` writes
     them beside its answer shapes.
   `printobserver-types/project.json`'s `schemas` and `schemas-update` targets run the
   `schemas` test of every crate that now declares schemas, and each declaring crate's
   reconciliation runs under its own `test` target so the gate runs it.

3. **The vision port is provider-neutral.** `NormalizedAlert` carries an `EventBody` and a
   `print: Option<ProviderPrint>` correlation in the shape the seam states;
   `printobserver-obico/src/normalize.rs` fills both from the body it read (`ProviderPrint`
   from the `print` object, as `Correlation` already computes it); its wire-field test in
   `printobserver-vision-api/tests/schemas.rs` states the new fields.

4. **The supervision core names no adapter's kind.** `printobserver-core/src/events.rs`'s
   `obico_print_id` and `alert_file_name` readers of the payload go; `resolve_print` reads
   `alert.print` (the store lookup keeps its present name until step 3 renames it); every
   `EventPayload::X(..)` construction in core, the server and the Obico ingress becomes
   `EventBody::of(&XPayload { .. })`; the Obico ingress's `correlation_of` reads
   `alert.print` too. Core's own journey suite drives `handle_event` with alerts whose
   kind is one **declared in core's test support** (a fixture payload type implementing
   `EventPayload` under a kind no crate ships, e.g. `test_provider_alert`) rather than
   with Obico's — which is the proof that core is provider-neutral, and what keeps step 2
   from touching these tests again. Core's tests may not depend on the Obico crate (the
   table admits no adapter edge into core, in any dependency table).

5. **The store persists the same bytes.** `printobserver-store-sqlite`'s `insert_event`
   writes `kind` from `body.kind` and `payload` as the JSON text of `body` — the same
   `{"kind":..,"payload":..}` text the enum's tagged form produced — and `event_from_row`
   reads the `EventBody` off the `payload` column; the `kind IN (...)` filter and the
   in-memory store filter by `EventKind`. The migrations journey seeds the events row's
   `payload` column with the **literal text 0.2.0 wrote** (not a value serialized from a
   type) and reads it back as the same kind and payload; it also seeds one row under a
   kind no crate declares and reads it back. The conformance suite that drives both store
   implementations re-matches to the seam.

6. **The codegen learns the open log**, in `tools/contract-codegen`:
   - `schemas.py`'s `load` reads every `*.json` under every immediate subdirectory of
     `schemas/` (the operations description still from the server's directory), refuses a
     type name declared under two directories, and refuses two schemas carrying the same
     `x-event-kind`; `TYPES_DIR` and the two-directory tuple go; the module doc says the
     schema set is keyed by type name across every declaring crate.
   - The model gains a shape for a JSON value of any form (the boolean schema `true`, or
     an empty object schema, is what `schemars` emits for `serde_json::Value` — note that
     `_fields` today silently drops a property whose schema is not a dict, so `payload`
     must be read explicitly), rendered as `serde_json::Value`, `object` and `unknown`.
   - The root set becomes the operations closure plus every schema carrying
     `x-event-kind`; the marker's value is read into the model as that declaration's kind.
   - Each emitter writes, beside `EventRecord`, the kind→payload-type table and the typed
     accessor the contract states (suggested spellings — yours to settle, stated in the
     change request: Rust a generated `EventPayloadKind` trait with `KIND` implemented per
     payload type and `EventRecord::payload_as::<P>()`; TypeScript an `EventPayloads`
     interface keyed by kind literal and `payloadOf(event, kind)`; Python an
     `EVENT_PAYLOAD_TYPES` mapping and `payload_of(event, kind)` with per-kind overloads).
   - The generated walks (`emit_walk` per client, and the example values `examples.py`
     builds) exercise the accessor over one known kind carrying that payload's example
     value and over one unknown kind.
   - Its own tests under `tools/contract-codegen/tests` drive generation end to end over a
     schema set with a marked payload declared under a third directory, a duplicate
     type name, a duplicate kind, and an envelope carrying an any-JSON field, and read the
     result back out of each emitted client.
   - The three clients are regenerated. `crates/printobserver-sdk/tests/integration.rs`
     and every other hand-written SDK test that matched `EventRecordKind` arms re-matches
     through the accessor; each SDK's tests exercise the table and the accessor over one
     known and one unknown kind, so each client's own coverage floor holds.

7. **Every remaining match site re-matches.** Beyond the sites above: `expiry.rs`,
   `actions.rs`, the server's `ingress.rs` and `reconcile.rs`; and the test files across
   `printobserver-core`, `printobserver-obico`, `printobserver-oneharness` (whose
   supervision tests build `EventRecord`s to render — an `EventBody` built directly, or a
   test-local payload type, since that crate may not depend on core),
   `printobserver-server`, `printobserver-store-api`, `printobserver-store-sqlite`,
   `printobserver` and `printobserver-vision-api`. About eight non-test files and
   twenty-eight test files name the old pair; the count is a reading of the base branch,
   not a bar.

8. **The documents follow.** `docs/reference/schemas.md` is regenerated the documented way
   (its generator in `tools/repo-checks/src/repo_checks/docs.py` says the set is "every
   type `printobserver-types` declares" — it now says the set is every type any crate
   declares under `schemas/<crate>/`); `docs/reference/architecture.md`'s entries for the
   crates this step touched say what each owns now; every touched crate's `//! Owns:` /
   `//! May depend on:` module comment is restated (the workspace check refuses one that
   does not say both). The dependency edges this step draws — `printobserver-obico` →
   `printobserver-core` (for `PortFailurePayload`, and later for the store traits) — are
   admitted by the layered rule in force today; draw no other.

## Why

The user is bootstrapping and maintaining many repositories through the `create-repo`
skill, and the modularity it produces is not buying what modularity is for: a split whose
units are "the types", "the data access" and "the core" makes every real change a change
to several packages and makes every package depend on code it does not use. printobserver
is the concrete case in hand, and the user found the first plan's cut short: it moved the
provider's wire types out of the center but left the center holding a closed enum with a
variant per domain's events — every domain's payload struct, `ObicoNotificationType`
included — so that adding one provider's event still edited the crate every other crate
builds against, and the supervision core still matched on Obico by name. In the user's
words: *until I pushed we were still going to centralize a bunch of stuff
unnecessarily.* This step is where that is undone: what stays central is the envelope
every domain writes under, and each domain owns its kinds.

## Acceptance criteria

- `printobserver-types` declares `EventKind`, `EventSource`, `EventBody`, `EventRecord`,
  the `EventPayload` trait and `event_schema_of` in the shapes the seam section states,
  declares no enum with a variant per event kind or per source, no list of kinds, and no
  `*Payload` type, `ObicoNotificationType`, `PortFailureSite` or `StartupOutcome`; `ImageRef`
  remains there.
- Each of the thirteen payload types implements `EventPayload` in the crate the table
  assigns as its owner and in no other crate, with `KIND` equal to the tag it was written
  under on the base branch; `ObicoNotificationType`, `PortFailureSite` and `StartupOutcome`
  are declared in their owners; each owner's schema reconciliation writes the payload's
  schema under `schemas/<owner>/` with an `x-event-kind` member equal to that `KIND`,
  and is green under that crate's `test` target.
- A test of the seam in `printobserver-types` shows: a payload read back under its own
  kind equals what was written; `read`/`payload_as` answer nothing for a payload type whose
  kind differs from the record's; an `EventRecord` carrying a kind no crate declares
  survives a serialize–parse round trip unchanged; the wire form of a record is the fields

## What

The second of four steps on one branch that redraws printobserver's crate graph by
domain. The previous step opened the event log and gave every event kind to its owner;
read the branch's commits and its report before starting, because this step builds on

central `printobserver-types` crate** into the crates that own them: the Obico wire types
and their sample bodies to the Obico adapter, the printer snapshots and ranges to the

Four consequences the table is drawn for, which the finished tree shows:

- A change to one provider's wire format **or to one provider's event payload** edits that
  provider's crate and rebuilds it and the composition roots. The reverse-dependency set
  of `printobserver-octoprint`, `printobserver-obico` and `printobserver-oneharness` is
  exactly `{printobserver-server, printobserver}`; of `printobserver-store-sqlite` the
  same.
- `printobserver-types` still sits under every crate — that is what a contract crate is —
  but nothing in it names a domain: no enum with a variant per provider or per domain's
  events, no list of kinds, no list of sources. A domain that adds an event kind, an
  aggregate or a source name edits its own crate and regenerates the clients; it edits
  nothing central. That is the test the sharpened `code_lands_in_the_domain_that_owns_it`
  rule applies, and this graph is drawn to pass it.
- The event log is **open**. A reader of the log — the store, the server, a client, a
  test — handles a kind it does not know explicitly rather than by exhaustive match: it
  carries the record through, filters by name, or reads a typed payload out of it and
  gets nothing back when the kind is another's. Exhaustive matching over the log is gone
  from this workspace, by design.
- The SDK contract is the schema set under `schemas/<crate>/<Type>.json`, keyed by type
  name across every declaring crate, and the codegen reads every crate directory; a type
  moving crates moves its schema file between directories and changes no generated line.
  The generated clients change in exactly one respect across the whole branch: they say
  what the server says about the log — the envelope is open, every domain's payload type
  is still emitted, and a kind→payload table with a typed accessor replaces the closed
  union.

### The event seam, which every step builds to

Declared in `printobserver-types` (module `event`, re-exported at the root). The names,
shapes and wire forms below are the contract; the exact error type an accessor answers,
the derive lists, and the constructor spellings are the implementer's, stated in the code's
own docs. Every crate that declares an event kind restates nothing from here: it imports
the trait and the envelope, and the **one authoritative source of a kind name is the
`KIND` const on the payload type that owns it** — the schema marker is written from that
const by the toolkit, the store column is written from it, and the clients' tables are
generated from the marker, with the drift gate (`check-generated`) going red when the
generated copy parts from the schema set.

```rust
/// The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the
/// domain that owns the event. Serializes as the bare string; schema: string, pattern
/// `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Ord + Hash, so a filter can hold a set of them.
pub struct EventKind(String);            // EventKind::new(impl Into<String>), as_str(), Display

/// Where an event came from, as the bare string each domain declares for itself.
/// The four names in use today are unchanged: "obico", "operator", "agent", "system".
pub struct EventSource(String);          // same shape as EventKind

/// One typed payload declared under a kind name, by the domain that owns it.
pub trait EventPayload: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema {
    const KIND: &'static str;
    fn kind() -> EventKind { EventKind::new(Self::KIND) }
}

/// The kind and the payload, as the log holds them: the pair `{"kind": .., "payload": ..}`.
pub struct EventBody { pub kind: EventKind, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
impl EventBody {
    pub fn of<P: EventPayload>(payload: &P) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error>;
    pub fn is<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> bool;                        // kind == P::KIND
    pub fn read<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>; // None: another's kind
}

/// One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it. Wire form unchanged:
/// `id`, `print_id`, `source`, `received_at`, `image`, `kind`, `payload`, `raw`.
pub struct EventRecord {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub print_id: Option<PrintId>,
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: Option<RawBytes>,
}
impl EventRecord {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &EventKind;
    pub fn payload_as<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>;
}

// In the schema toolkit (`contract`): the schema of an event payload is the schema its type
// emits plus one top-level member, `"x-event-kind": P::KIND`. Nothing writes that member by
// hand; the owning crate's schema test writes and reconciles the file through this.
pub fn event_schema_of<P: EventPayload>() -> serde_json::Value;
```

The thirteen kind names are wire and storage contract and do not change: `obico_failure_alert`,
`obico_printer_notification`, `malformed_external_event`, `action_requested`,
`action_executed`, `action_rejected`, `intervention_expired`, `supervision_session_opened`,
`supervision_session_closed`, `agent_assessment`, `operator_acknowledgement`,
`port_failure`, `startup_reconciliation` — each the `KIND` const of the payload type the
table above assigns to its owner. Kind names are unique across the workspace, and the
codegen is the cross-domain check: it refuses two schemas carrying the same `x-event-kind`.

Two other shapes carry the seam across boundaries and are part of it:

```rust
// printobserver-vision-api — what an adapter hands the supervision domain. Core reads the
// correlation here and never a provider's payload by kind.
pub struct NormalizedAlert {
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: RawBytes,
    pub image_url: Option<String>,

    /// when the alert is about a print at all.
    pub print: Option<ProviderPrint>,
}
pub struct ProviderPrint { pub id: i64, pub file_name: Option<String> }

// The store's own draft of an event (in printobserver-store-api until step 3, in
// printobserver-core from then on):
pub struct EventDraft { pub print_id: Option<PrintId>, pub source: EventSource,
                        pub received_at: Timestamp, #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
                        pub raw: Option<RawBytes> }
// HistoryQuery.kinds becomes Vec<EventKind>; empty still means every kind.
```

**Persistence is unchanged, and that is the fact the whole cut rests on.** The SQLite
`events` table already holds `kind TEXT` as the bare kind name and `payload TEXT` as the
JSON text of the pair `{"kind":"<kind>","payload":{...}}` (what the closed enum's tagged
form serialized to); the open store writes the identical text — `kind` from `body.kind`,
`payload` as the JSON of `body` — and reads a record back off the `payload` column. A row
written by 0.2.0 reads under 0.3.0 unchanged, and a row whose kind no crate of this
workspace declares reads back as an `EventRecord` carrying it. The `source` column already
holds the bare source string.

**The generated clients' contract**, produced by `tools/contract-codegen` from the schema set:
`EventRecord` in each client is the envelope — `kind: string` and an opaque `payload`
(Rust `serde_json::Value`, Python `object`, TypeScript `unknown`) beside the fields above;
`EventSource` is a string; every payload type whose schema carries `x-event-kind` is
emitted as a standalone type whether or not an operation reaches it; each client carries a
generated table from kind name to payload type and a typed accessor that answers the
payload as that type for a matching kind and nothing for another, with no other runtime
validation than today's clients perform; a kind from a newer server flows through. The
package names — the `printobserver-sdk` crate, the `printobserver-sdk` wheel,
`@printobserver/sdk` — do not change.

The dependency rule is stated as this table, not as layers. `repo-policy.toml`'s
`[crates]` section becomes an explicit per-crate list of the workspace crates each crate
may depend on (across `dependencies`, `dev-dependencies` and `build-dependencies`), and

and any table row naming a crate the workspace lacks — the step that draws an edge is the
step that admits it in the table, so the check-repo tier proves the target graph rather
than a later step. Until step 3 replaces it, the layered rule in force today permits every
edge the steps before it draw.

## Why

The user is bootstrapping and maintaining many repositories through the `create-repo`
skill, and the modularity it produces is not buying what modularity is for: a split whose
units are "the types", "the data access" and "the core" makes every real change a change
to several packages and makes every package depend on code it does not use. printobserver
is the concrete case in hand — a change to one printer provider's wire format edits the
central types crate and so rebuilds and re-tests all thirteen crates — and refactoring it
against the rule the previous node put into the skill is how the user confirms that rule
says something a real repository can act on. This step is the half of that refactor with
the clearest owners: a provider's wire types belong to the provider, a port's vocabulary
to the port.

**A wait written against a full command line never ends, because one of those command
lines is yours.** That is a different defect from the one above — it wedges your own
dispatch rather than somebody else's — and it is why `pgrep -f` cannot be waited on.
`pgrep -f` matches its pattern against every process's whole argv and excludes exactly one
process — itself — never the shell that invoked it. So any pattern naming the thing you are
waiting for is, by construction, a substring of the command line of the shell doing the
waiting: `until ! pgrep -f "just gate"` matches its own loop and never exits, and so does
the same loop written against `llmlint-judge.sh`, `scripts/fetch-corpus.sh`, or
`publish-branch`. That is a defect in the polling mechanism rather than a fact about gates,
so it applies to every wait you write.

night: seven instances of one defect. A crozier corpus audit waited in `until ! pgrep -f

**Wait with a sentinel file.** Background the whole command you are waiting on — one
command, so that what you waited on is what you meant to run — and poll for a file only
that invocation can write:

    ( just test > /tmp/check.$$.log 2>&1; echo $? > /tmp/check.$$.exit ) &
    until [ -f /tmp/check.$$.exit ]; do sleep 20; done

**A process must finish inside the turn that started it.** Backgrounding is how you wait

shows up a turn later as a sentinel that never appeared and a recipe terminated by

because a worker reaches for backgrounding exactly when a command is slow enough to
threaten the turn — here the judged lint tier and a whole test tier, which are the two
runs a node most needs to have made. So run a slow check in the foreground, or background
it and wait out its sentinel before your turn ends; never end a turn intending to read a
result on the next one.

### The event seam, which every step builds to

Declared in `printobserver-types` (module `event`, re-exported at the root). The names,
shapes and wire forms below are the contract; the exact error type an accessor answers,
the derive lists, and the constructor spellings are the implementer's, stated in the code's
own docs. Every crate that declares an event kind restates nothing from here: it imports
the trait and the envelope, and the **one authoritative source of a kind name is the
`KIND` const on the payload type that owns it** — the schema marker is written from that
const by the toolkit, the store column is written from it, and the clients' tables are
generated from the marker, with the drift gate (`check-generated`) going red when the
generated copy parts from the schema set.

```rust
/// The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the
/// domain that owns the event. Serializes as the bare string; schema: string, pattern
/// `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Ord + Hash, so a filter can hold a set of them.
pub struct EventKind(String);            // EventKind::new(impl Into<String>), as_str(), Display

/// Where an event came from, as the bare string each domain declares for itself.
/// The four names in use today are unchanged: "obico", "operator", "agent", "system".
pub struct EventSource(String);          // same shape as EventKind

/// One typed payload declared under a kind name, by the domain that owns it.
pub trait EventPayload: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema {
    const KIND: &'static str;
    fn kind() -> EventKind { EventKind::new(Self::KIND) }
}

/// The kind and the payload, as the log holds them: the pair `{"kind": .., "payload": ..}`.
pub struct EventBody { pub kind: EventKind, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
impl EventBody {
    pub fn of<P: EventPayload>(payload: &P) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error>;
    pub fn is<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> bool;                        // kind == P::KIND
    pub fn read<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>; // None: another's kind
}

/// One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it. Wire form unchanged:
/// `id`, `print_id`, `source`, `received_at`, `image`, `kind`, `payload`, `raw`.
pub struct EventRecord {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub print_id: Option<PrintId>,
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: Option<RawBytes>,
}
impl EventRecord {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &EventKind;
    pub fn payload_as<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>;
}

// In the schema toolkit (`contract`): the schema of an event payload is the schema its type
// emits plus one top-level member, `"x-event-kind": P::KIND`. Nothing writes that member by
// hand; the owning crate's schema test writes and reconciles the file through this.
pub fn event_schema_of<P: EventPayload>() -> serde_json::Value;
```

## Why

The user is bootstrapping and maintaining many repositories through the `create-repo`
skill, and the modularity it produces is not buying what modularity is for: a split whose
units are "the types", "the data access" and "the core" makes every real change a change
to several packages and makes every package depend on code it does not use. printobserver
is the concrete case in hand, and its central store port is the sharpest instance: one
trait every domain's persistence goes through, in a crate every consumer of the store
depends on, so a new column for one aggregate is a change everything rebuilds against.
This step is the half of the refactor that removes the central data-access package the
user named — the supervision domain's records, its identifiers and the interfaces it
needs live with the supervision domain, its most-read record stops naming one provider,
and what remains central is only what every domain and every client must agree on and
nothing a domain adding a concept has to edit.

### Operational notes for this host

**Run only the checks that exercise what you changed.** The tests that cover the code
you touched, the lint that reads your diff — and nothing wider. The repository's own
automation runs the full bar downstream on the change this work becomes: a `pre-push`
hook where that repository publishes locally, the host's required checks where it
publishes remotely. Neither is waiting for you to have run it first, so running it here
spends twenty to forty minutes of this dispatch learning what the merge path reports
anyway. That is measured rather than estimated: one node in this workstream spent about
84 minutes on three rounds of everything its repository could run, to reach lint findings
a diff-scoped run reports in two.

**Pick those checks from your change, and take the narrowest scope each one supports.**
One test module over the whole suite; the lint over your diff over the lint over the
tree. A repository's own fast deterministic tier is a fine choice when it is what
exercises your change — its `just --list` says which recipe that is — and a poor one when
you reached for it because it was the widest thing available. When a check you ran
reports something, fix that and run **that check** again; nothing here asks you to re-run
its neighbours to confirm, and a wider tier cannot re-check a finding it never made.

**A dispatch that changed nothing tracked owes none of them.** When your deliverable is a
document, a report, or an answer, there is no changed code for those checks to exercise
and you are complete without them — decide that from what the repository shows, never
because running them is slow or inconvenient. `git status` reporting nothing to commit is
then a correct and complete outcome, not a problem to solve by writing a file nobody
asked for.

**Never signal a process you did not identify by PID, and a PID you got from a pattern is
still a pattern kill.** Several managers share this host, and their dispatches, drivers,
publications and test servers run under the same few binary names — `just`, `node`,
`python`, `onepipeline-api` — so a kill by name knows nothing about *whose* work it
matched. The distinction is the tool rather than the pattern: `pgrep` and `ps` **read**,
and either spelling of them is fine, `pgrep -x` included; `pkill` **signals**, and it is
never the answer here, in any spelling. `-x` is the trap, because it reads as the careful
one — `pkill -f 'just gate'` at least needs a narrowing pattern, while `pkill -x just`
takes every `just` on the machine. Reading the table first and piping the pids into `kill`
is no way around it: that is the same pattern kill with more steps.

Two workers reached that place from different directions on 2026-08-24, while another
manager's dispatch had been live over an hour. One ran `pkill -TERM -x just`. The other
ran `ps -eo pid,args | grep 'onepipeline-api serve' | awk '{print $1}' | while read pid;
do kill "$pid"; done` — which obeys the letter of every paragraph below and does the same
damage, because `just dag-ui` and the e2e suites both spawn that server and a pytest run's
were alive at that moment.

**The one process you may signal is one you started yourself, so capture its PID as you
start it:**

    cmd & MYPID=$!
    kill "$MYPID"

Anything you did not start belongs to somebody. Read what it is, report what you found,
and leave it running.

**A wait written against a full command line never ends, because one of those command
lines is yours.** That is a different defect from the one above — it wedges your own
dispatch rather than somebody else's — and it is why `pgrep -f` cannot be waited on.
`pgrep -f` matches its pattern against every process's whole argv and excludes exactly one
process — itself — never the shell that invoked it. So any pattern naming the thing you are
waiting for is, by construction, a substring of the command line of the shell doing the
waiting: `until ! pgrep -f "just gate"` matches its own loop and never exits, and so does
the same loop written against `llmlint-judge.sh`, `scripts/fetch-corpus.sh`, or
`publish-branch`. That is a defect in the polling mechanism rather than a fact about gates,
so it applies to every wait you write.

That has wedged four workers here, and then two more workers and the manager itself in one
night: seven instances of one defect. A crozier corpus audit waited in `until ! pgrep -f
'scripts/fetch-corpus.sh'` with no fetch running at all — the only two matches were its own
polling shell and the manager's diagnostic shell — and waited until it was interrupted. A

command, so that what you waited on is what you meant to run — and poll for a file only
that invocation can write:

    until [ -f /tmp/check.$$.exit ]; do sleep 20; done

**A process must finish inside the turn that started it.** Backgrounding is how you wait
on a slow command *within* one turn, which is why the launch and the wait sit together in
that example — both halves belong to the same turn. What does not survive is a background
process left running when the turn ends: nothing carries it across, and the launch gives
you no sign of that, because it succeeded and the turn then ended normally. The loss
shows up a turn later as a sentinel that never appeared and a recipe terminated by
signal, with the whole run to pay for again. It bites hardest where it is most tempting,
because a worker reaches for backgrounding exactly when a command is slow enough to
threaten the turn — here the judged lint tier and a whole test tier, which are the two
runs a node most needs to have made. So run a slow check in the foreground, or background
it and wait out its sentinel before your turn ends; never end a turn intending to read a
result on the next one.

### The event seam, which every step builds to

Declared in `printobserver-types` (module `event`, re-exported at the root). The names,
shapes and wire forms below are the contract; the exact error type an accessor answers,
the derive lists, and the constructor spellings are the implementer's, stated in the code's
own docs. Every crate that declares an event kind restates nothing from here: it imports
the trait and the envelope, and the **one authoritative source of a kind name is the
`KIND` const on the payload type that owns it** — the schema marker is written from that
const by the toolkit, the store column is written from it, and the clients' tables are
generated from the marker, with the drift gate (`check-generated`) going red when the
generated copy parts from the schema set.

```rust
/// The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the
/// domain that owns the event. Serializes as the bare string; schema: string, pattern
/// `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Ord + Hash, so a filter can hold a set of them.
pub struct EventKind(String);            // EventKind::new(impl Into<String>), as_str(), Display

/// Where an event came from, as the bare string each domain declares for itself.
/// The four names in use today are unchanged: "obico", "operator", "agent", "system".
pub struct EventSource(String);          // same shape as EventKind

/// One typed payload declared under a kind name, by the domain that owns it.
pub trait EventPayload: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema {
    const KIND: &'static str;
    fn kind() -> EventKind { EventKind::new(Self::KIND) }
}

/// The kind and the payload, as the log holds them: the pair `{"kind": .., "payload": ..}`.
pub struct EventBody { pub kind: EventKind, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
impl EventBody {
    pub fn of<P: EventPayload>(payload: &P) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error>;
    pub fn is<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> bool;                        // kind == P::KIND
    pub fn read<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>; // None: another's kind
}

/// One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it. Wire form unchanged:
/// `id`, `print_id`, `source`, `received_at`, `image`, `kind`, `payload`, `raw`.
pub struct EventRecord {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub print_id: Option<PrintId>,
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: Option<RawBytes>,
}
impl EventRecord {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &EventKind;
    pub fn payload_as<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>;
}

// In the schema toolkit (`contract`): the schema of an event payload is the schema its type
// emits plus one top-level member, `"x-event-kind": P::KIND`. Nothing writes that member by
// hand; the owning crate's schema test writes and reconciles the file through this.
pub fn event_schema_of<P: EventPayload>() -> serde_json::Value;
```

steps.task:
## What

The first of four steps on one branch that redraws printobserver's crate graph by
domain. This step **opens the event log**: the closed `EventKind`/`EventPayload` pair in
`printobserver-types` — one variant per domain's events, so that the supervision core
matched on Obico's kinds by name and every domain's payload struct sat in the crate every
other crate builds against — becomes an envelope with an open kind name and an opaque
payload, and **every event kind moves to the crate of the domain that owns it**. The
supervision core reacts to the vision port's `NormalizedAlert` and to nothing an adapter
declares; the store persists exactly the bytes it persists today; the contract codegen
learns the open envelope, reads every `schemas/<crate>/` directory, and still emits every
domain's payload type to the three clients. No type that is not an event kind moves in
this step — the provider wire types, the printer vocabulary, the supervision records and
the store port are the later steps' — so that this step is one thing: who owns the log's
kinds, and what a reader of the log may assume.

### The target crate graph, which every step of this node builds toward

This node's four steps share one branch and one contract: the graph below, and the event
seam stated after it. A step builds toward it and never past it; a step that finds it wants
a different cut — a missing item, a different owner, a better name for something a
criterion fixes — surfaces a proposal to the manager over the ask seam and keeps building
against this one, because the steps after it and the change request's reviewer are reading
this table. A shared interface is never changed unilaterally.

Thirteen crates become twelve. `printobserver-store-api` is retired from the workspace:
release automation publishes every workspace crate, so it stays on crates.io at `0.2.0`,
is never yanked, and is never published again. The manager measured its consumers before
this plan was written: crates.io's reverse-dependency listings for `printobserver-types`
(11), `printobserver-store-api` (5) and the three other port crates name only crates of
this workspace; a GitHub code search for `printobserver-types` across the owner's
repositories returns only this repository; no other checkout registered on this host
names them. So the API this refactor breaks has no consumer outside this tree, and the
one release it cuts is a pre-1.0 breaking release (`feat!` → `0.3.0`). Do not re-derive
that measurement.

| Crate | Owns after the refactor | May depend on (workspace crates, every dependency table) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `printobserver-types` | **The cross-domain contract, and only that** — what every domain and every client must agree on, and nothing a domain adding a concept has to edit. The identity rule: the `identifier!` macro (exported), `IdentifierError`, the UUID-v7 rule, and the three identifiers the envelope reaches — `PrintId`, `EventId`, `ImageId`. The representation rules: `Timestamp`, `RawBytes`, `FileName`, `Reported<T>` and `Range`. The event envelope: `EventKind`, `EventSource`, `EventBody`, the `EventPayload` trait, `EventRecord`, and `ImageRef` (the envelope's image handle). The schema toolkit (`contract`: `Sample`, `TypeContract`, `WireField`, `wire_fields`, `schema_of`, `event_schema_of`, and a `declared` set naming only this crate's own types). The `serde`, `serde_json` and `schemars` re-exports. Its module doc says it is the vocabulary every domain and every client must agree on, and that a type belongs here only if adding or changing one domain's concept does not require editing it. | — |
| `printobserver-printer-api` | The printer port, plus the printer domain's vocabulary: `PrinterSnapshot`, `HeaterSnapshot`, `JobSnapshot`, `PrinterState`, `Adjustable` and `AdjustableError`, the seven `*_RANGE` constants, `RangedField` and `RANGED_FIELDS`. | `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-vision-api` | The vision port: `NormalizedAlert` (now carrying an `EventBody` and a provider-neutral `ProviderPrint` correlation), `FetchedImage`, `VisionError`, `VisionPort`; and the event kind `malformed_external_event` (`MalformedExternalEventPayload`) — a body this port could not read, written down. | `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-supervisor-api` | The supervisor port, plus its vocabulary: `SupervisionSession`, `SessionPhase`, `AgentAssessment`, `Confidence`; and the event kinds `supervision_session_opened` and `supervision_session_closed`. | `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-core` | **The supervision domain.** Its logic, as now; its own records: `PrintRecord` (whose external correlation field is `provider_print_id`), `ManifestNarrowing`, `JobManifest`, `PrintContext`, `Intervention`, `InterventionOutcome`, `ImageRecord`, `SafetyEnvelope`, `EffectiveBounds`, `PolicyDecision`, `RejectionReason`, `PrintAction`, `ActionKind`, `Actor`, `ActorClass`, `ExecutionOutcome`, `AcknowledgementDisposition`, `ActionRequest`, `ActionRecord`, and its own identifiers `ActionId` and `InterventionId` (minted through the exported macro); its event kinds `action_requested`, `action_executed`, `action_rejected`, `intervention_expired`, `agent_assessment`, `operator_acknowledgement`, `port_failure` (with `PortFailureSite`); its event-source names `system`, `operator`, `agent`; and the persistence interfaces it needs, one trait per aggregate rather than one trait for everything, with the shapes those methods carry — `EventDraft`, `HistoryQuery`, `ImageLookup`, `SettleOutcome`, `AuditPage`, `StoreError`, `DEFAULT_HISTORY_WINDOW`, `MAX_HISTORY_LIMIT`, `resolve_history_limit` — and the four behavioural facts of the history read, stated where the traits are. | `printobserver-types`, `printobserver-printer-api`, `printobserver-vision-api`, `printobserver-supervisor-api` — and **no adapter crate**, which is what keeps the graph acyclic |

| `printobserver-obico` | The Obico adapter: its nine wire types (`ObicoEventType`, `ObicoFailureAlert`, `ObicoFailureEvent`, `ObicoFailureEventType`, `ObicoNotificationEvent`, `ObicoPrintInfo`, `ObicoPrinterInfo`, `ObicoPrinterNotification`, `ObicoTimestamp`) and the webhook sample bodies; its event kinds `obico_failure_alert` and `obico_printer_notification` with `ObicoNotificationType`; its event-source name `obico`; the vision port implementation; and the webhook ingress, which writes through the supervision domain's store traits. | `printobserver-vision-api`, `printobserver-core`, `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-oneharness` | The oneharness adapter — unchanged. | `printobserver-supervisor-api`, `printobserver-types` |
| `printobserver-store-sqlite` | The SQLite implementation (and the in-memory one beside it) of core's store traits. | `printobserver-core`, `printobserver-supervisor-api`, `printobserver-printer-api`, `printobserver-types` |

| `printobserver-sdk` | The generated Rust client. | — |
| `printobserver` | The command — unchanged. | `printobserver-server`, `printobserver-sdk`, `printobserver-types` |

Four consequences the table is drawn for, which the finished tree shows:

- A change to one provider's wire format **or to one provider's event payload** edits that
  provider's crate and rebuilds it and the composition roots. The reverse-dependency set
  of `printobserver-octoprint`, `printobserver-obico` and `printobserver-oneharness` is
  exactly `{printobserver-server, printobserver}`; of `printobserver-store-sqlite` the
  same.
- `printobserver-types` still sits under every crate — that is what a contract crate is —
  but nothing in it names a domain: no enum with a variant per provider or per domain's
  events, no list of kinds, no list of sources. A domain that adds an event kind, an
  aggregate or a source name edits its own crate and regenerates the clients; it edits
  nothing central. That is the test the sharpened `code_lands_in_the_domain_that_owns_it`
  rule applies, and this graph is drawn to pass it.
- The event log is **open**. A reader of the log — the store, the server, a client, a
  test — handles a kind it does not know explicitly rather than by exhaustive match: it
  carries the record through, filters by name, or reads a typed payload out of it and
  gets nothing back when the kind is another's. Exhaustive matching over the log is gone
  from this workspace, by design.
- The SDK contract is the schema set under `schemas/<crate>/<Type>.json`, keyed by type
  name across every declaring crate, and the codegen reads every crate directory; a type
  moving crates moves its schema file between directories and changes no generated line.
  The generated clients change in exactly one respect across the whole branch: they say
  what the server says about the log — the envelope is open, every domain's payload type
  is still emitted, and a kind→payload table with a typed accessor replaces the closed
  union.

### The event seam, which every step builds to

Declared in `printobserver-types` (module `event`, re-exported at the root). The names,
shapes and wire forms below are the contract; the exact error type an accessor answers,
the derive lists, and the constructor spellings are the implementer's, stated in the code's
own docs. Every crate that declares an event kind restates nothing from here: it imports
the trait and the envelope, and the **one authoritative source of a kind name is the
`KIND` const on the payload type that owns it** — the schema marker is written from that
const by the toolkit, the store column is written from it, and the clients' tables are
generated from the marker, with the drift gate (`check-generated`) going red when the
generated copy parts from the schema set.

```rust
/// The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the
/// domain that owns the event. Serializes as the bare string; schema: string, pattern
/// `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Ord + Hash, so a filter can hold a set of them.
pub struct EventKind(String);            // EventKind::new(impl Into<String>), as_str(), Display

/// Where an event came from, as the bare string each domain declares for itself.
/// The four names in use today are unchanged: "obico", "operator", "agent", "system".
pub struct EventSource(String);          // same shape as EventKind

/// One typed payload declared under a kind name, by the domain that owns it.
pub trait EventPayload: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema {
    const KIND: &'static str;
    fn kind() -> EventKind { EventKind::new(Self::KIND) }
}

/// The kind and the payload, as the log holds them: the pair `{"kind": .., "payload": ..}`.
pub struct EventBody { pub kind: EventKind, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
impl EventBody {
    pub fn of<P: EventPayload>(payload: &P) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error>;
    pub fn is<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> bool;                        // kind == P::KIND
    pub fn read<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>; // None: another's kind
}

/// One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it. Wire form unchanged:
/// `id`, `print_id`, `source`, `received_at`, `image`, `kind`, `payload`, `raw`.
pub struct EventRecord {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub print_id: Option<PrintId>,
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: Option<RawBytes>,
}
impl EventRecord {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &EventKind;
    pub fn payload_as<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>;
}

// In the schema toolkit (`contract`): the schema of an event payload is the schema its type
// emits plus one top-level member, `"x-event-kind": P::KIND`. Nothing writes that member by
// hand; the owning crate's schema test writes and reconciles the file through this.
pub fn event_schema_of<P: EventPayload>() -> serde_json::Value;
```

The thirteen kind names are wire and storage contract and do not change: `obico_failure_alert`,
`obico_printer_notification`, `malformed_external_event`, `action_requested`,
`action_executed`, `action_rejected`, `intervention_expired`, `supervision_session_opened`,
`supervision_session_closed`, `agent_assessment`, `operator_acknowledgement`,
`port_failure`, `startup_reconciliation` — each the `KIND` const of the payload type the
table above assigns to its owner. Kind names are unique across the workspace, and the
codegen is the cross-domain check: it refuses two schemas carrying the same `x-event-kind`.

Two other shapes carry the seam across boundaries and are part of it:

```rust
// printobserver-vision-api — what an adapter hands the supervision domain. Core reads the
// correlation here and never a provider's payload by kind.
pub struct NormalizedAlert {
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: RawBytes,
    pub image_url: Option<String>,
    /// The provider's own identifier for the print this alert is about, and the file it named,
    /// when the alert is about a print at all.
    pub print: Option<ProviderPrint>,
}
pub struct ProviderPrint { pub id: i64, pub file_name: Option<String> }

// The store's own draft of an event (in printobserver-store-api until step 3, in
// printobserver-core from then on):
pub struct EventDraft { pub print_id: Option<PrintId>, pub source: EventSource,
                        pub received_at: Timestamp, #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
                        pub raw: Option<RawBytes> }
// HistoryQuery.kinds becomes Vec<EventKind>; empty still means every kind.
```

**Persistence is unchanged, and that is the fact the whole cut rests on.** The SQLite
`events` table already holds `kind TEXT` as the bare kind name and `payload TEXT` as the
JSON text of the pair `{"kind":"<kind>","payload":{...}}` (what the closed enum's tagged
form serialized to); the open store writes the identical text — `kind` from `body.kind`,
`payload` as the JSON of `body` — and reads a record back off the `payload` column. A row
written by 0.2.0 reads under 0.3.0 unchanged, and a row whose kind no crate of this
workspace declares reads back as an `EventRecord` carrying it. The `source` column already
holds the bare source string.

**The generated clients' contract**, produced by `tools/contract-codegen` from the schema set:
`EventRecord` in each client is the envelope — `kind: string` and an opaque `payload`
(Rust `serde_json::Value`, Python `object`, TypeScript `unknown`) beside the fields above;
`EventSource` is a string; every payload type whose schema carries `x-event-kind` is
emitted as a standalone type whether or not an operation reaches it; each client carries a
generated table from kind name to payload type and a typed accessor that answers the
payload as that type for a matching kind and nothing for another, with no other runtime
validation than today's clients perform; a kind from a newer server flows through. The
package names — the `printobserver-sdk` crate, the `printobserver-sdk` wheel,
`@printobserver/sdk` — do not change.

The dependency rule is stated as this table, not as layers. `repo-policy.toml`'s
`[crates]` section becomes an explicit per-crate list of the workspace crates each crate
may depend on (across `dependencies`, `dev-dependencies` and `build-dependencies`), and
`tools/repo-checks`'s workspace check refuses any workspace edge the table does not admit
and any table row naming a crate the workspace lacks — the step that draws an edge is the
step that admits it in the table, so the check-repo tier proves the target graph rather
than a later step. Until step 3 replaces it, the layered rule in force today permits every
edge the steps before it draw.

### What this step does

1. **The seam, in `printobserver-types`.** `event.rs` declares `EventKind`, `EventSource`,
   the `EventPayload` trait, `EventBody`, `EventRecord` and `event_schema_of` exactly in
   the shape the seam section states; the enum `EventPayload`, the enum `EventKind` with
   its `ALL`, the enum `EventSource`, and every `*Payload` struct, `ObicoNotificationType`,
   `PortFailureSite` and `StartupOutcome` leave this crate. `ImageRef` stays: the envelope

## Why

The user is bootstrapping and maintaining many repositories through the `create-repo`
skill, and the modularity it produces is not buying what modularity is for: a split whose
units are "the types", "the data access" and "the core" makes every real change a change

variant per domain's events — every domain's payload struct, `ObicoNotificationType`

words: *until I pushed we were still going to centralize a bunch of stuff
unnecessarily.* This step is where that is undone: what stays central is the envelope
every domain writes under, and each domain owns its kinds.

### The event seam, which every step builds to

Declared in `printobserver-types` (module `event`, re-exported at the root). The names,
shapes and wire forms below are the contract; the exact error type an accessor answers,
the derive lists, and the constructor spellings are the implementer's, stated in the code's
own docs. Every crate that declares an event kind restates nothing from here: it imports
the trait and the envelope, and the **one authoritative source of a kind name is the
`KIND` const on the payload type that owns it** — the schema marker is written from that
const by the toolkit, the store column is written from it, and the clients' tables are
generated from the marker, with the drift gate (`check-generated`) going red when the
generated copy parts from the schema set.

```rust
/// The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase snake_case, declared by the
/// domain that owns the event. Serializes as the bare string; schema: string, pattern
/// `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`. Ord + Hash, so a filter can hold a set of them.
pub struct EventKind(String);            // EventKind::new(impl Into<String>), as_str(), Display

/// Where an event came from, as the bare string each domain declares for itself.
/// The four names in use today are unchanged: "obico", "operator", "agent", "system".
pub struct EventSource(String);          // same shape as EventKind

/// One typed payload declared under a kind name, by the domain that owns it.
pub trait EventPayload: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema {
    const KIND: &'static str;
    fn kind() -> EventKind { EventKind::new(Self::KIND) }
}

/// The kind and the payload, as the log holds them: the pair `{"kind": .., "payload": ..}`.
pub struct EventBody { pub kind: EventKind, pub payload: serde_json::Value }
impl EventBody {
    pub fn of<P: EventPayload>(payload: &P) -> Result<Self, serde_json::Error>;
    pub fn is<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> bool;                        // kind == P::KIND
    pub fn read<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>; // None: another's kind
}

/// One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it. Wire form unchanged:
/// `id`, `print_id`, `source`, `received_at`, `image`, `kind`, `payload`, `raw`.
pub struct EventRecord {
    pub id: EventId,
    pub print_id: Option<PrintId>,
    pub source: EventSource,
    pub received_at: Timestamp,
    pub image: Option<ImageRef>,
    #[serde(flatten)] pub body: EventBody,
    pub raw: Option<RawBytes>,
}
impl EventRecord {
    pub fn kind(&self) -> &EventKind;
    pub fn payload_as<P: EventPayload>(&self) -> Option<Result<P, serde_json::Error>>;
}

// In the schema toolkit (`contract`): the schema of an event payload is the schema its type
// emits plus one top-level member, `"x-event-kind": P::KIND`. Nothing writes that member by
// hand; the owning crate's schema test writes and reconciles the file through this.
pub fn event_schema_of<P: EventPayload>() -> serde_json::Value;
```

## Why

The user is bootstrapping and maintaining many repositories through the `create-repo`
skill, and the modularity it produces is not buying what modularity is for: a split whose
units are "the types", "the data access" and "the core" makes every real change a change
to several packages and makes every package depend on code it does not use. printobserver
is the concrete case in hand — a change to one printer provider's wire format edits the
central types crate and so rebuilds and re-tests all thirteen crates — and refactoring it
against the rule the previous node put into the skill is how the user confirms that rule
says something a real repository can act on. This step is the half of that refactor with
the clearest owners: a provider's wire types belong to the provider, a port's vocabulary
to the port.
